units.explanation: update_link_info replaces parameterized SELECT with string-interpolated URL list: The single hunk rewrites the SELECT in update_link_info from a parameterized IN (?) query to an f-string that interpolates raw URL values (x[3]) into the SQL, introducing a SQL-injection sink for externally-sourced URLs.

Replace string-interpolated SQL with parameterized query in update_link_info: The single hunk removes an f-string that spliced user-controlled URLs into a SELECT, replacing it with bound placeholders, which is the core authorization/injection concern of this PR.

Replace parameterized/Identifier SQL with string-formatted SQL, introducing SQL injection: All five hunks remove psycopg2's parameterized queries and SQL/Identifier quoting in favor of .format() string interpolation of user-controlled db_name, db_username, db_pwd and username, turning previously safe identifier handling into injectable SQL across the create/delete/exists paths.

Harden postgres_cluster driver against SQL injection via parameterized queries and Identifier: All driver hunks replace string-formatted SQL with psycopg2 parameterized queries and SQL/Identifier composition, closing the injection vector for db_name, db_username and db_pwd.
Mark bad-username tests as xfail now that injection is prevented: Both test hunks add xfail markers because the previously-injectable usernames are now safely quoted, so the old 'syntax error' assertions no longer hold.

Remove parameterized to_sql() generation from the Lucene query parser: These hunks delete the _next_param helper and all to_sql() methods and change QueryParser.parse to return a repr()-based SQL string with no bound parameters, so the parser no longer emits parameterized SQL.
Adapt query builders to the new single-return parser and drop bound qvars: Both from_params call sites now consume the single string returned by parser.parse and set qvars to an empty dict, so the previously parameterized q values are no longer bound and instead flow into the SQL text.

Convert Lucene query parser to emit parameterized SQL (named %(...)s placeholders) instead of inlined literals: These hunks add the _next_param helper, to_sql() methods on the AST nodes, and the new parse() return contract that together replace string-interpolated values with bound parameters, eliminating the SQL-injection surface in the search query.
Adapt Alerts and Blackouts from_params to consume the new (sql, params) tuple and seed qvars: Both call sites unpack the new two-value return and populate qvars from parsed_vars so the bound parameters flow into the executed query.
Update queryparser tests to assert parameterized SQL and add SQL-injection prevention cases: All test hunks rewrite assertions to the new (sql, params) contract and add explicit injection-prevention checks for quotes and SQL keywords.

Remove thread ownership pre-check from run-creation endpoints: All four hunks delete the same duplicated `existing_thread` ownership guard (and its now-unused ThreadORM import) from the create/stream/wait run endpoints, so they are one access-control concern.

Add thread ownership check to run-creation endpoints: The import plus the three identical ownership guards in create_run, create_and_stream_run, and wait_for_run all enforce the same access-control rule (reject a thread not owned by the authenticated user) before any run is prepared.
Update unit test session mocks for the new thread lookup: These unit tests change mock_session.scalar from a single return_value to a side_effect list so the first scalar call returns the thread-ownership result and the second returns the assistant, matching the new endpoint ordering.
Update integration test DummySession to answer thread query: The integration test's DummySession.scalar now returns a thread row for 'from thread' statements so the new ownership check passes before the assistant/run lookups.
Add E2E tests for thread user isolation: This new manual-auth E2E suite verifies the cross-user 404 behavior across thread get/search/list/mutate and the run/stream/wait endpoints, directly exercising the ownership guard added in the source.

Remove per-user ownership check from delete_api_key and rely on route-level auth: The CRUD function, the API route, and the CLI caller are all changed together to drop the user_id ownership check, so any authenticated user can now delete any API key by ID.

Enforce per-user ownership on API key deletion: The CRUD function, the HTTP route, and the CLI caller are all updated together to pass the authenticated user's id and reject deletion of keys owned by another user, closing a cross-user IDOR on DELETE /api_key/{id}.
Regression test for cross-user API key deletion: Adds a test that a second user cannot delete a first user's API key and that the key survives, directly exercising the new ownership guard.

Add a `where_in` Jinja2 filter that builds a SQL IN list with quote-escaping: The new `where_in` function, its registration on the SandboxedEnvironment in `BaseTemplateProcessor.__init__`, and its unit test all implement and verify one new SQL-templating filter whose output is interpolated into user-controlled SQL, so they share the same injection/escaping authorization concern.

Authorization of parameterized sub-queries via _load_query: The new param_query path reuses get_query_results/_load_query, so the existing org + has_access(view_only) checks are the access-control gate for the newly added parameterized queries.
Parameter substitution into query text (injection surface): replace_query_parameters and prepare_parameterized_query splice user-supplied param strings directly into SQL text, an injection/authorization-relevant behavior that must be reviewed together.
Extraction of param_query references from user query: extract_query_params parses the attacker/user-controlled query to derive which sub-queries and params are loaded, feeding the authorization and injection paths above.
Tests for parameterized query handling: The new test hunks exercise extract_query_params, prepare_parameterized_query and replace_query_parameters, documenting the intended (and security-relevant) behavior of the param feature.

Core QuerySet.explain() API and SQL compilation: These hunks together add the public QuerySet.explain() entry point, the Query state flags, the compiler's EXPLAIN prefix injection and result flattening, and the base operations/feature contract that all backends build on.
MySQL backend EXPLAIN support: These hunks configure MySQL's EXPLAIN prefix, supported formats, the TEXT→TRADITIONAL alias, and the EXTENDED fallback for pre-5.7 versions.
PostgreSQL backend EXPLAIN support: These hunks configure PostgreSQL's EXPLAIN prefix, supported formats, and pass-through of arbitrary EXPLAIN options (COSTS, BUFFERS, etc.).
SQLite backend EXPLAIN support: This hunk sets the SQLite-specific EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN prefix, enabling the base explain_query_prefix to work without format support.
Tests for QuerySet.explain(): These hunks add the dedicated test suite for explain(), register 'explain' in the manager proxy-methods list, and suppress MySQLdb informational warnings during tests.

New /ajax/lookup route lacks authentication and per-view authorization: The new ajax_lookup endpoint and its route registration expose model data without the @login_required decorator or the _create/_edit/_export-style is_accessible/can_* checks that every other data route enforces.
AJAX loader wiring into forms, fields, widgets and model config: These hunks together build the form_ajax_refs pipeline (loader creation, field types, widget rendering, and passing refs into scaffold_form) that feeds the lookup endpoint and the create/edit forms.
Test fixtures and AJAX test suite: Test-only changes that exercise the new lookup endpoint and form rendering, including a change to the default async test database URI.

Adds a new Memory API endpoint (list + delete) restricted to superusers: These hunks together wire up a new MemoryViewSet with a serializer, URL registration, and imports that expose translation-memory entries via the REST API, gating all access behind is_superuser and the memory.delete permission.
Adds API tests for the new Memory endpoint (superuser 200/403 and delete 204): These test hunks exercise the new MemoryViewSet's authorization behavior (superuser vs non-superuser list, and superuser delete) and import the Memory model they assert against.

New config API endpoints with per-user queryset scoping: The new AbstractConfigViewSet subclasses and their get_queryset methods define the read/write authorization boundary for the new config endpoints.
Add get_owner_object to AbstractChangeConfig for ownership checks: This method is the hook WgerOwnerObjectModelViewSet calls to resolve the owning user for create/update on the new config viewsets.
Config serializers and shared CONFIG_FIELDS constant: These serializers and the shared field tuple define the data exposed by the new endpoints, including the slot_config FK used for ownership.
Altered PermissionDenied message in shared viewset: This hunk modifies the error message raised by the shared ownership check used by all WgerOwnerObjectModelViewSet subclasses.

New exporters API endpoints (list/retrieve/run/download) with permission enforcement: These hunks together add the serializers, viewsets, and URL routes that expose exporter listing, execution, and file download, all gated by the `permission` attribute checked in EventPermission.
Extend multiexport task to support Device and TeamAPIToken authentication: These hunks modify the multiexport task signature, the OrganizerUserTask base class, and add get_events_with_permission to Device/TeamAPIToken so that non-user API tokens can trigger multi-event exports with proper permission scoping.
Make paid_only field required in mail exporter: Changes the order status filter field from optional to required, affecting validation behavior of the mail exporter.
Tests for exporters API and permission coverage: New and updated tests that verify exporter listing, validation, execution, download, and permission enforcement for the new API endpoints.

Core API HITL endpoints with DAG-scoped authorization: These hunks add the public HITL routes, their datamodels, and register them on the authenticated router, where each endpoint enforces requires_access_dag on TASK_INSTANCE.
Execution API HITL endpoints under JWT auth: These hunks add the execution-API HITL routes and datamodels and mount them on the JWT-protected authenticated router, with no per-resource authorization beyond the TI id.
HITLDetail ORM model, registry and DB migration: These hunks define the new hitl_detail table, register the model, and bump the migration head to create it.
Task SDK HITL client, comms and datamodels: These hunks add the HITL payload/result types, the HITLOperations client, and wire them into the supervisor/triggerer message unions.
Standard provider HITL operator, trigger and exceptions: These hunks add the HITLOperator/ApprovalOperator, the HITLTrigger, supporting exceptions, and provider registration.
airflowctl generated HITL datamodels: These hunks add the generated HITLDetail and UpdateHITLDetailPayload schemas used by the CLI client.

New POST /api/dashboards/<id>/fork endpoint gated by edit_dashboard permission: The handler, its route registration/import, and the test all exercise the same new authorization surface: a permission-gated endpoint that forks a dashboard.
Dashboard.fork and Widget.copy model methods used by the fork endpoint: These model methods implement the data-copy logic invoked by the new handler and are the data-integrity counterpart to the authorization gate.

Introduce RealmExport model and migration replacing RealmAuditLog for export records: These hunks define the new RealmExport model, its status/type constants, the migration, and the model export, which all other authorization changes depend on.
Authorize export request: admin-only, rate limit, and create RealmExport row: The view enforces require_realm_admin, the 5-per-7-day rate limit, and quota checks before creating a RealmExport row and queueing the deferred work.
Authorize export deletion by realm-scoped RealmExport lookup and status checks: delete_realm_export and do_delete_realm_export gate deletion on admin role and the row's status, operating on the new RealmExport row.
Worker processes queued export by RealmExport id with status guard: The deferred worker resolves the RealmExport row by id, enforces the REQUESTED status guard, and runs the export for the realm.
Replace module-level EXPORT_* constants with RealmExport class constants: These hunks migrate export-type comparisons and imports to the new RealmExport constants, keeping consent/full-export authorization logic consistent.
export_realm_wrapper and stats now operate on a RealmExport row: The wrapper signature, stats return value, and audit-log creation are refactored to read/write the RealmExport row that carries authorization-relevant status and consent type.
Add RealmExport to export serialization config and imports: These hunks register the zerver_realmexport table and its fields in the export config and add supporting imports for serializing export rows.
Management export command creates a RealmExport row instead of audit log: The CLI export path now records the export as a RealmExport row with the chosen type, aligning its authorization/consent semantics with the API path.
Update tests to assert RealmExport-based authorization behavior: Test hunks update mocks and assertions to the new RealmExport row, status, and export-type constants that the authorization logic now uses.

ShareLink model definition and database migration: These hunks define the new ShareLink model and its migration, including the permission-creation data migration that grants sharelink permissions to users/groups with add_document.
ShareLink API viewset, serializer, filter, and permission enforcement: These hunks wire the ShareLink CRUD API with PaperlessObjectPermissions, ObjectOwnedOrGrantedPermissionsFilter, and the serializer that auto-generates the slug, all enforcing object-level access control.
Public share link file-serving view (unauthenticated): SharedLinkView serves a document file to unauthenticated users based solely on slug lookup and expiration check, with no authentication or permission classes.
Django admin registration for ShareLink: Registers ShareLink in the Django admin with GuardedModelAdmin, exposing list display and filters for created, expiration, and owner.
Tests for share link creation, permissions, and public access: Tests verify that share link creation requires authentication, that listing share links enforces change_document permission, and that the public view correctly handles valid, invalid, and expired slugs.
Management exporter test count adjustments for new ShareLink model: Updates expected ContentType and Permission counts in exporter tests to account for the new ShareLink model and its four permissions.
Comment typo fix in urls.py: Corrects a typo in a comment (Frontent → Frontend); no authorization impact.

Removal of proxy-admin-only guards on user_role modification in user update endpoints: Both hunks delete the 403 checks that restricted user_role changes (single and bulk/all-users) to PROXY_ADMIN, leaving only the weaker can_user_call_user_update self-or-admin check.
Removal of admin-only guard on key spend modification in /key/update: The condition that required _check_key_admin_access when data.spend changed was dropped, so only max_budget changes remain admin-gated.
Pure reformatting of assignments and comments (no authorization logic change): These hunks only reflow line-wrapped assignments and comments without altering any access-control condition.

Restrict user_role modification to proxy admins in user update endpoints: Both hunks add 403 guards in the single-user and bulk user update paths to prevent non-admin callers from changing user_role.
Extend key-update admin check to cover spend modifications: Hunks #1 and #2 widen the existing max_budget admin-only check to also require admin access when spend is changed, and update the route label.
Cosmetic reformatting of key-management code (no logic change): Hunks #0, #3, #4, #5, #6 only re-wrap existing expressions/assignments across lines without altering behavior or authorization.

global_spend_logs: admin-only spend endpoint now accepts an api_key query param and builds a raw SQL query from it: Both hunks modify the same /global/spend/logs handler: one adds the api_key query parameter and the other branches on it to run a string-concatenated SQL query against the new per-key view, so the authorization (admin-only claim vs. only user_api_key_auth dependency) and SQL-injection concerns are inseparable.
check_view_exists: create MonthlyGlobalSpendPerKey view exposing per-key spend: This hunk adds the DB view that the global_spend_logs per-key branch reads, so it defines the data exposure surface (per-key spend) that the authorization review must consider.
